clause.text: 1.01. Distribution Right. The distribution right shall be limited to all countries and all of their territories and possessions within the continent known as South America ("Territory") (Exhibit "B" attached hereto). Distributor agrees that the Products, including the name Snotarator ™ Nasal Aspirator (the "Brand") are the sole property of the Company and Distributor has no interest whatsoever in such Brand and Products, and Distributor shall use the Brand and Products only for so long as the rights granted hereby remains in full force and effect. Distributor shall not take any actions, or aid or assist any other party to take any actions that would infringe upon, harm or contest the proprietary rights of Company in and to the Brand and Products. Distributor shall not assign the rights granted in this Section 1.01 without the prior written consent of the Company.

Distributor shall not assign the rights granted in this Section 1.01 without the prior written consent of the Company.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants an exclusive distribution right to Distributor without any duration limit, minimum-performance expectation, or lapse mechanism, which materially deviates from the [no-exclusivity] position's acceptable fallback (exclusivity capped at twelve months and lapsing if minimum performance targets are unmet). The territorial scope is bounded by the named South America Territory and named Products, but the lack of any time or performance constraint is a limited, negotiable deviation rather than a full prohibition breach. The assignment restriction (prior written consent only) aligns reasonably with the [assignment-change-of-control] fallback's consent language, so it does not independently raise the risk beyond medium. The Brand and Products ownership language is consistent with each party retaining its existing property, so no separate IP-ownership risk is triggered.

citations.excerpt: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. A change of control is not an assignment for the purposes of this clause.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.
reviews.verification_reason: Several defects. (1) Risk level does not follow: the [no-exclusivity] position has 'Risk if absent: high', and the clause grants open-ended exclusivity with no term or performance targets—i.e., the position is absent, not merely deviated from. Labeling this a 'limited, negotiable deviation' and capping risk at medium contradicts the cited playbook risk rating. (2) Mischaracterization of the assignment clause: the clause requires prior written consent with no 'not unreasonably withheld' qualifier and no change-of-control carve-out. The reviewer says it 'aligns reasonably with the [assignment-change-of-control] fallback's consent language,' which is untrue—the fallback's key elements (reasonableness standard and change-of-control non-assignment) are missing, so it is not aligned; at most it partly tracks the preferred/fallback consent requirement. (3) Unsupported claim: 'The Brand and Products ownership language is consistent with each party retaining its existing property.' The clause says the Brand and Products are the Company's sole property and the Distributor has no interest; no playbook source on IP ownership is cited, so this is outside the provided playbook positions and is not verifiable. (4) The rationale does not clearly separate what the clause states from what policy requests in a way that supports the medium risk conclusion. The quotation of the fallback is verbatim and the territorial/product scope observation is supported by the clause text, but the overall risk determination and the assignment alignment claim are not grounded.

reviews.rationale: This clause establishes a purchase-order mechanics procedure (ordering, acceptance, and shipment scheduling) and contains no minimum purchase, volume, or share-of-requirements commitment. The only relevant playbook position, no-minimum-commitment, expresses the preferred policy that the ordering party is under no minimum obligation and pays only for what it orders. The clause is consistent with that position, so no deviation exposure is present. Positions on confidentiality, force majeure, renewal, and payment timing govern unrelated obligations and are not applied here. Note that the clause does not state an explicit no-minimum disclaimer, but it also imposes no minimum commitment, so the relevant protection is effectively met.

The rationale properly distinguishes what the clause states (mechanics, no explicit disclaimer) from what policy requests (no minimum commitment / pay-for-actual), and notes the absence of an explicit no-minimum disclaimer while explaining that no minimum is imposed. The 'Risk: low' conclusion for the no-minimum-commitment position follows from the fact that the clause contains no minimum commitment, so the risky term is absent. No suggested fallback was provided, consistent with the cited playbook fallback not being needed. The claim that unrelated positions (confidentiality, force majeure, renewal, payment timing) are not applied is accurate—they were not cited as evidence. All claims are supported.

These departures go beyond the bounded force-majeure protection the playbook requires. Separately, the clause unilaterally disclaims only Company's liability for incidental, special, or consequential damages; the liability policy requires a mutual exclusion, so this is a material deviation from the preferred position.

The relevant playbook position (termination-for-convenience) contemplates a mutual right with 30 days' (preferred) or 60 days' (fallback) prior written notice, without penalty beyond accrued amounts. clause.text: 4.01 Patent Infringement. Company agrees, at its own expense, to indemnify, defend and hold harmless each Distributor and its customers from and against every expense, damage, cost and loss (including attorneys' fees incurred) and to satisfy all judgments and decrees resulting from a claim, suit or proceeding insofar as it is based upon an allegation that any Product or any part thereof furnished by Company or any process which is practiced in the customary use of the Product is or has been infringing upon any patent, copyright or proprietary right, if Company is notified promptly of such claim in writing and given authority, and full and proper information and assistance (at Company's expense) for the defense of same. In case any Product, or any part thereof, if such suit is held to constitute an infringement and the use of said Product or part is enjoined, Company shall, in its sole discretion and at its own expense, either procure for the indemnitee the right to continue using said Product or provide or procure for the Distributor a similar product.

In case any Product, or any part thereof, if such suit is held to constitute an infringement and the use of said Product or part is enjoined, Company shall, in its sole discretion and at its own expense, either procure for the indemnitee the right to continue using said Product or provide or procure for the Distributor a similar product.

reviews.rationale: The clause is a one-way IP infringement indemnity covering allegations that the Company's Products or their customary-use processes infringe patents, copyrights, or proprietary rights, with prompt-notice and defense-cooperation conditions. This substantially aligns with the [ip-infringement-indemnity] preferred scope (defend and indemnify against third-party IP infringement claims). The deviation is in the remedy: the preferred position requires payment of damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement, while the clause obligates the Company to satisfy judgments and provides only discretionary equitable relief (procure the right to continue use or provide a similar product). It omits both a refund-of-fees option and an express obligation to pay settlement amounts, which is a limited, negotiable deviation from the preferred/fallback remedy set. Note the clause states no cap on this indemnity, but the [ip-infringement-indemnity] preferred and fallback positions likewise do not require a cap, so no-cap is not itself a policy deviation; the mutual-indemnity position concerns a different subject matter (indemnities for a party's own breach or negligence) and is not applied here.

citations.excerpt: Supplier shall defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe that third party's intellectual property rights, and shall pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.

Supplier shall defend Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe that third party's intellectual property rights, and shall at its option procure the right to continue using the affected item, modify it so it is non-infringing, or refund the fees paid for it.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Supplier shall defend Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe that third party's intellectual property rights, and shall at its option procure the right to continue using the affected item, modify it so it is non-infringing, or refund the fees paid for it.
reviews.verification_reason: All contract claims are supported by the clause: the indemnity is one-way (Company indemnifies Distributor/customers), covers patents/copyrights/proprietary rights for Products and customary-use processes, conditions on prompt notice and defense cooperation, obligates satisfaction of judgments, and provides only discretionary equitable relief (procure right to continue use or provide a similar product) with no refund option and no express settlement-payment obligation. The policy claims accurately reflect the cited preferred and fallback positions, and the stated no-cap point correctly notes that neither playbook position requires a cap. The rationale properly distinguishes clause language from policy requirements, and the risk level of medium follows from the limited, negotiable remedy deviation. The suggested fallback matches the cited [ip-infringement-indemnity] fallback text verbatim.

reviews.rationale: The clause contains a one-way indemnity: the Distributor indemnifies the Company, but the Company assumes no reciprocal indemnity obligation. The mutual-indemnity position contemplates each party indemnifying the other for third-party claims arising from its own breach or negligence (or, at fallback, its gross negligence or willful misconduct), subject to a liability cap. The instant indemnity is uncapped and lacks any third-party-claim framing or limitation, and the Company provides no corresponding protection. However, the indemnity is at least scoped to the Distributor's fault or negligence in its use of the mark and distribution of the Products, which confines exposure rather than creating open-ended liability. This is a limited deviation from the mutual preferred position that is negotiable, so medium rather than high. The clause does not concern IP infringement indemnification by a supplier for the Services/Deliverables, so the ip-infringement-indemnity position is not applicable.

citations.excerpt: Each party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party against third-party claims to the extent arising from its own breach of this Agreement or its negligence, subject to the limitations of liability set out in this Agreement.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Each party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party against third-party claims to the extent arising from its own gross negligence or willful misconduct, subject to the limitations of liability set out in this Agreement.
reviews.verification_reason: The clause supports the unilateral indemnity claim (Distributor indemnifies Company; no Company obligation to Distributor). The mutual-indemnity playbook is correctly characterized as reciprocal and capped, with the fallback limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct subject to a liability cap. The rationale properly distinguishes contract text (uncapped, no third-party-claim framing, scoped to Distributor's fault/negligence) from policy, and cites the preferred position rather than the fallback as the standard. The medium risk follows because the clause only deviates partially (scoped to fault/negligence) rather than being fully open-ended. The suggested fallback matches the playbook fallback text verbatim. The ip-infringement-indemnity point is a reasonable applicability conclusion not contradicted by the evidence.
